newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan sees movement in easing Israel water row.
newsitem.headline: Jordan sees movement in easing Israel water row.

text.p: Jordan and Israel have agreed to resolve a dispute over water rights to the parched kingdom under their 1994 peace treaty, Jordanian Information Minister Samir Mutawae said on Saturday.
The proposal was agreed at a meeting on Thursday between King Hussein and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
Jordan's Crown Prince Hassan had cancelled talks on Tuesday with Netanyahu because of the water dispute.
It relates to an accord that was to help bring an extra 50 million cubic metres of water a year to the kingdom within a year of the peace treaty taking effect.

"The Israeli side proposed providing the amount in two stages, the first to provide 25 million cubic metres (annually) immediately and the second 25 million cubic metres (phase) after three years," said Mutawae.
Under the deal, which awaits final signature, Israel would undertake the second stage only once storage projects were ready, Mutawae said.

Jordan's Foreign Minister Fayez al-alTarawnah said on Friday the meeting had not resolved the dispute, but added it had helped to bring viewpoints together although technicalities had still to be resolved.

Technical experts from both sides will meet soon to work on details of projects to help raise the kingdom's storage capacity to enable it to secure its water rights, Mutawae told reporters after a regular cabinet meeting.
The government had previously portrayed the peace accord as a platform to solve its chronic water shortage by eventually ovtaining 235 million cubic metres of additional water each year.
Numerous schemes were mentioned to achieve this, including dams and a desalination plant which have yet to materialise.
